idiom_name: dynamic import() of plugin packages, validated at load time
implementation_notes: The classic loader, contract and factory classes collapse into the module system: a plugin is a package or a file whose entry point the host resolves at run time with await import(pathToFileURL(entry).href) (or require for CommonJS), and the package's main/exports fields act as its descriptor while exports also encapsulates everything else. What replaces the participants is a plain object plus a registry: the plugin exports an object with lifecycle functions, the host keeps a Map of loaded plugins and hands each setup() a context object that exposes only the published services, and the module cache becomes the cache - so a real unload means terminating a worker or process. Because the language has no types at runtime, the shape check has to be written by hand or with a schema library, and the classic structure only reappears when the host needs isolation.
pitfalls: The ESM module cache is keyed by URL and cannot be cleared, so hot reload needs a worker/process restart or a cache-busting query string; require.cache deletion only works while nothing holds the old export.
A dynamic specifier that cannot be resolved statically breaks bundlers or makes them inline the wrong thing, so plugin entry points must be resolved at runtime from a real path or package name.
A plugin that brings its own copy of a shared dependency creates duplicate instances of the same module, so state and instanceof checks disagree between host and plugin.
